takeaway: Iliacus and psoas insert on the lesser trochanter and flex the hip; piriformis, the obturators, gemelli and gluteus medius and minimus attach to the greater trochanter.

question.text: A 50-year-old man is undergoing a total hip replacement. The operating surgeon takes a lateral approach to the joint. Which of the following anatomical structures does not attach to the greater trochanter?
question.say: A fifty-year-old man is undergoing a total hip replacement. The operating surgeon takes a lateral approach to the joint. Which of the following anatomical structures does not attach to the greater trochanter?

lines.text: A lateral approach to the hip brings the surgeon onto the greater trochanter.
The greater trochanter sits on the lateral side of the femur.
Piriformis, obturator internus and externus, gluteus medius and minimus, and the gemelli all attach here.
The lesser trochanter is on the medial side of the proximal femur.
Iliacus and psoas attach to this prominence, and they flex the hip.
So poor iliacus never reaches the greater trochanter.
lines.say: (laugh) So poor iliacus never reaches the greater trochanter.

lines.text: The muscle that does not attach there is iliacus.
